title: Shwedagon Pagoda
summary: The Shwedagon Pagoda is the gilded stupa crowning Singuttara Hill in Yangon, Myanmar, and the country's most revered Buddhist shrine. Legend dates it to the Buddha's lifetime, but research suggests it was first built between the 6th and 10th centuries CE. Rulers raised it in stages to 99 m by 1774, and a new umbrella in 1871 brought it to 112 m.

uncertainty.note: Start is the midpoint of 'first built between the 6th and 10th centuries AD' (UNESCO tentative list); the legend of a 2,600-year-old foundation is not used. End is the present: the stupa stands.

reviewer_note: No model written: UNESCO's tentative list gives the height (99 m after 1774, 112 m after the 1871 umbrella) and a 5.66 ha platform, but no university, museum or heritage page opened gives the stupa's base diameter, so the plan-dimension rule is not met. Least sure of the start date: 'between the 6th and 10th centuries AD' is a wide window and the 750 midpoint is a convenience. Tentative-list coordinates (N16.798356 E96.149705) and OSM agree to about 100 m.

phases.description: Stupa renovated by King Byinya U; the earliest reliable record cited by the source.
About fifty years later King Binnyagyan raised the stupa to 295 feet (approximate year from the source's 'fifty years later').
Queen Shin Sawbu's gold donations give the stupa its present shape and form.
King Hsinbyushin replaces the hti after earthquake damage, raising the monument to its present height of 330 feet.
Stupa stands on its hilltop platform, repaired after earthquakes in the 17th and 18th centuries.

materials.material: gold plating on the exterior, from Queen Shin Sawbu's donation of her weight in gold (90 pounds)
